hints: Breadth-first search naturally groups nodes by depth.
Reset the running sum at the start of every level.
Consume exactly the current queue length, enqueue children, and retain the final level sum.
After the last iteration, the saved sum contains exactly all nodes at maximum depth.
editorial: Traverse one breadth-first level at a time. Reset the answer before consuming that level, then enqueue every child. When the queue becomes empty, the most recently completed level is the deepest and its sum is the answer. The independent oracle walks the serialized tree level by level without constructing TreeNode objects.
